About me

Different stages.
Same curiosity.

I've always been fascinated by people—how they think, behave, and experience the world around them.

Long before I became a designer, I spent nearly a decade as a radio show host, connecting with audiences I would never meet. Every show meant understanding what people needed in that moment, what would keep them engaged, and what would leave them feeling something.

Back then, I never called it user research or human-centred design.

Turns out, there was already a name for it.

When I decided to pursue a Master's in UX Design, it never felt like starting over. It felt like changing the tools for something I'd been practising all along.

✦

A snapshot from one of my radio shows. Where it all started.

What shaped me

New places, new people, new perspectives.
